### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **10** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-comment.object.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a7a135dc267f0d154aca453f098c49ce8aac550c`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **10** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-comment.object.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a7a135dc267f0d154aca453f098c49ce8aac550c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cc8e23feb1e10626f8bf96878cb8c58dcc38338c` — the merge of head `1060ed3e74306c46a60e51745479a418806475bf` into base `a7a135dc267f0d154aca453f098c49ce8aac550c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cc8e23feb1e10626f8bf96878cb8c58dcc38338c && git checkout cc8e23feb1e10626f8bf96878cb8c58dcc38338c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a7a135dc267f0d154aca453f098c49ce8aac550c 1060ed3e74306c46a60e51745479a418806475bf && git checkout -B drift-repro a7a135dc267f0d154aca453f098c49ce8aac550c && git merge --no-ff 1060ed3e74306c46a60e51745479a418806475bf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a7a135dc267f0d154aca453f098c49ce8aac550c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a7a135dc267f0d154aca453f098c49ce8aac550c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1060ed3e74306c46a60e51745479a418806475bf`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23268 (body + all 8 comments, ruling of record 6159300530 letter A, dev report 6164903067), PR #23441 body, its 52-file list and the net diff against `main` at the head, and the head's check-runs (read once). Not read: the dispatch order, the dispatching seat's conclusions. No worktree, build, test or gate re-run; `record-recognisers.mjs --template` was the only command run in the repo.

**Check-runs on the head (read once, 2026-10-14):** every completed run is `success` — Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Lint & Repo Gates and its 8 lint/typecheck jobs, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, Build Docs, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, the four claim/card guards, Test Core 1/6, 2/6, 5/6, 6/6. **In progress at read time: Test Core (3/6) and Test Core (4/6)** — named here as in progress, not judged; the adopting seat reads their conclusions before the queue. Skipped (conditional, not failures): Console Pin Gate, Dogfood matrix shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance. The `check:platform-checklist` exit 1 the dev reports locally is not a head check-run and is not judged here.

### ① Derived judgments

Ruling 6159300530 item 1 binds: retire the key on v18 with an ADR-0087 entry, refuse at the located spot with "delete the key", census-class the stored rows, and take the lint rules, the posture gate's external branch, the ledger row, the two example objects, the five doc pages and the QA item's external clause with it; `crossTenantAccess` hint stops pointing at it. Each accept-set / public-surface change the diff implies, judged:

1. **`ObjectSchema.externalSharingModel` → `retiredKey(OBJECT_EXTERNAL_SHARING_MODEL_REMOVED)`** (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`). Accept set narrows: every former enum value (and any other value) is refused at path `externalSharingModel` with the key-first prescription; `tsc` fails first via `ServiceObject`. The tombstone route (not strict deletion) is **right** for a `strictObject` whose key must keep its ledger row and carry a prescription (playbook route; `rls.priority` precedent the ledger note cites). The prescription names what still works (`sharingModel`, explicit shares, `publicSharing`) and closes with the house `os migrate meta --from 17` sentence — **right**.
2. **Every door that parses an object now refuses it**: `ObjectSchema.create()`, `defineStack` (`STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` / 422), `getMetadataTypeSchema('object')` (the `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/:name` binding), and — because the schema parse runs before the lint discipline defers anything — the `?mode=draft` door too. The REST pin (`packages/rest/src/meta-object-owd-gate.test.ts`) re-pins the three doors on a pair the retired ordering rule ADMITTED (`private`/`private`), so the refusal is the key, not the posture. **Right**, and the draft-door refusal is a deliberate, named widening of the 422 relative to the old external-wider rule (which drafts deferred); it follows from the tombstone and is recorded in the QA item.
3. **D2 conversion `object-external-sharing-model-removed`** (protocol 18, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'`, order 64, `surface: 'object.externalSharingModel'`, lossless `stripKeys` over `objects[]`, fixture with a control object). `retiredAfter` matches the neighbouring step-18 entries at the head (`17.7.0`). Census class **`registered` with a mechanical strip** — **right**: the PR body's reasoning (Studio offered the select; `saveMetaItem` persisted it against the closed enum) means stored `object` rows can carry it, and the pin replays `applyConversionsToStoredItem('object', …)` to show the strip heals them. `not-required` would have been wrong here.
4. **Registrations**: `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` gains `data/Object:externalSharingModel`; D3 entry `object-external-sharing-model-retired` (surface without backticks, replacement, reason naming the D2 id, acceptance criteria); `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment order 96 in `registry.ts.template`; `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` inserted by identifier. Changeset carries `<!-- adr-0087: registered object-external-sharing-model-removed, object-external-sharing-model-retired -->`. **Right.** The `retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts` JOIN gains the conversion — **right** (the pin would otherwise go red; the dev reports it did and fixed it).
5. **Liveness ledger** `object.json`: `planned` → `dead`, `authorWarn` dropped, `verifiedAt` 2026-10-14, note cites the measurement tree and the tombstone anchor; README `object` row records the route; `state-counts/object.md` 53/0/0/1/0 = 54. **Right** — the tombstone keeps the key in the walked shape, so the row stays rather than leaving (the #19054 strict-deletion precedent does NOT apply). `Spec property liveness` is green on the head.
6. **Generated surface**: `authorable-surface/data.json` → `data/Object:externalSharingModel [RETIRED]`; the three reference pages regenerate to `never | optional | [REMOVED] …`. **Right** (the `check:generated` family sits under Lint & Repo Gates, green).
7. **`@objectstack/lint` public surface narrows**: `SECURITY_EXTERNAL_WIDER` and the rule `security-external-wider-than-internal` removed from `validate-security-posture.ts` and `index.ts`; `security-owd-alias` loses its `externalSharingModel` branch but SURVIVES for `sharingModel` — **right**: the ruling's "the alias rule … go with it" is read as the rule's external reader, not the rule, because the alias rule's internal reader is still live (ADR-0090 D4) and deleting it would widen the accept set on an unparsed intake. Module-private `OWD_WIDTH` goes with its only user. On an unparsed intake the key now reports as `liveness-dead-property` (the lint liveness pin flips the real-ledger case to the `dead` branch). **Right.** `authoring-rules.ts` D7 block count 14 → 13 is a comment-only follow of the removal.
8. **`@objectstack/plugin-security` `objectPostureGate`**: R1 compares `sharingModel` alone; the external half of R1 goes; `OWD_WIDTH` kept for the internal comparison. Behaviour narrows only on bodies that can no longer reach the gate (the schema refuses them first). **Right**; R2 stays retired as before (#8310).
9. **Examples**: `showcase_account` and `showcase_announcement` drop the key; `security/index.ts`, `positions.ts`, `coverage.ts`, `showcase_tour_security.md` stop describing an external dial. **Right** (ruling item 1 names the two objects). `@objectstack/example-showcase` is `private: true` — no changeset owed.
10. **Docs** (non-governed): `permissions/sharing-rules.mdx` section rewritten to "External principals — no external org-wide default", `permissions/authorization.mdx` (3 passages), `protocol/objectql/security.mdx`, `docs/design/permission-model.md` (2 passages), plus the three regenerated reference pages. Each now states the ADR-0095 `EXTERNAL`-rung reading, matching ruling item 2's sentence. `content/docs/releases/**` untouched (the drift bot flags 11 release-owned pages as affected; they are read-only and correctly left). **Right.**
11. **QA item** `access-security.owd-save-gate` revision 5: the Studio external-wider clause goes; the refusal/admit/shipped-declarations clauses are rewritten to the tombstone's 422 on every door, the admit without the key, and "no retired key shipped"; the seal clauses are unchanged; `surface` `mixed` → `api`; the new source anchor `object.zod.ts#OBJECT_EXTERNAL_SHARING_MODEL_REMOVED` names a constant the diff defines; history row 5 added, revision 4 row preserved. **Right.**
12. **Ruling item 3 (`publicSharing` untouched)**: the `publicSharing` schema and policy are not changed. The one edit near it is the strict-guidance string for a MIS-NESTED `publicSharing.externalSharingModel`, which previously steered the author "one level up" to the now-dead key — it now says the key is removed. **Right**; leaving the old text would have prescribed a refused key.
13. **Ruling item 5 (cloud seat)**: the PR body names `os migrate meta --stored` for the cloud seat's v18 stored preview. **Right.**
14. **Neighbouring text**: `crossTenantAccess` retirement hint no longer names the key (ruling item 1); `execution-context.zod.ts` `audience` doc comment; `protocol.ts` authoring-gate docblock; `sys-comment.object.ts` prescription and its pin. Comment-only; **right**. `execution-context.zod.ts` and `protocol.ts` are in other seats' in-flight claims; the claim comment cleared them as comment-only ordinary concurrency and the single-writer guard is green.
15. **New pin** `object-external-sharing-model-retirement.test.ts` (repo project, listed in `vitest.repo-tests.json`): schema, registry binding, `create()`, `defineStack` with control, every value, walked shape, mis-nested guidance, `@ts-expect-error` channel, stored-row seam, boot door with a lit control, per-object notices + idempotence, load-path retirement, the three registrations, and a tree-scoped absence walk with anti-vacuity floors and per-entry exclusion reasons (no allowlist file). The exclusion set is structural and each entry's job is to spell the key. **Right.**
16. **Tests re-pinned rather than deleted** where the key was a control: CLI integration/nightly fixtures move their warned-row control to `tool.outputSchema` (`experimental`); `lint-liveness-properties.test.ts` moves the planned-with-opt-in control to `page.print` and narrows the opt-in anti-vacuity with its reason; `solution-blueprint.test.ts` swaps the undeclared sibling to `publicSharing`; the dogfood guest-grants file drops the one fixture object that declared the key (ruling C on #23266 already said the guest reads neither key, so the case loses nothing). **Right.** The REST door-order pin `[ADR-0131 D6] … ahead of lint AND R1, hatch open` is removed because its body was external-wider; the same door order is still pinned by the surviving `[#7674] R1` widening case (`an env overlay that widens … is refused by the package door before R1, hatch open`) — acceptable, no coverage lost.

Nothing in the diff widens any accept set. No governed surface (`docs/adr/**`, `skills/**`, `.claude/**`, `.objectui-sha`, `content/docs/releases/**`) is touched; Governed Surface Queue Guard is green.

Residual mentions at the head, judged: `packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts:712` keeps `externalSharingModel: keep` — **right**, the ADR-0106 D1 table classifies every key of the walked shape and the tombstone keeps the key in it (its test is pinned against the live shape); `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts:493` is a comment that already says the key "is not read here for anyone (#23268)" — **right** as it stands; `skills/objectstack-data/references/lint-rules.md:23` still lists the removed rule — governed, see ③.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23268-external-sharing-model-retired.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/lint: minor`, `@objectstack/plugin-security: patch`, title `feat(spec)!:`, **BREAKING** banner, FROM → TO table (the key and the `SECURITY_EXTERNAL_WIDER` import), the one-line fix, the prescription verbatim, the retirement kit, the NOT MEASURED out-of-repo consumer line, and the ADR-0087 `registered` disposition naming both ids.

- The breaking narrowing is published as `minor` on the `18.0.0-next.0` line, which is this repo's launch-window convention: the head's pending changesets for the same class (`23082-view-data-api-provider-retired.md`, `15204-s8-catalog-row-objects-retired.md`) use `feat(spec)!:` + `minor` + a registered disposition, and the `Check Changeset` job's "Require an ADR-0087 disposition on a declared-breaking changeset" and "Guard against accidental major bumps (launch window)" steps both passed on the head. **Matches.**
- `@objectstack/lint: minor` — a removed export and rule id: a published-surface narrowing; the FROM → TO row names it. **Matches** (same convention).
- `@objectstack/plugin-security: patch` — one internal branch of a gate goes; no export changes. **Matches.**
- Packages touched without a changeset: `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/dogfood` (tests and comments only), `@objectstack/example-showcase` (private). None owes one. **Right.**
- `Clause-②:` line: present in the PR body (`Clause-②: no`) and in the changeset (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`), matching the claim (6161609217) and triage's grading (`Clause-②: no`, contract-tier review). **Matches.**

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6164903067, `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer there. `deviations`, each answered:

1. *File surface beyond the claim's list* (stale tests across cli/lint/rest/plugin-security/plugin-audit/dogfood/spec, `vitest.repo-tests.json`, `lint/src/index.ts`, `check-doc-security-posture.mjs`, `docs/design/permission-model.md`, the `publicSharing` guidance string) — **answered, accepted**: each is a consequence of the retirement (a test authoring the key as a control, the export's barrel, a comment, a design doc restating D11, and a guidance string that prescribed the dead key); each is listed in the PR body; none is a governed or single-writer path; the single-writer guard is green.
2. *`object-schema-fls-references.ts` keep table NOT edited* — **answered, right** (①, residual mentions): the tombstone keeps the key in the walked shape the table is pinned against; the claim listed the file on the assumption of a strict deletion.
3. *Lint witnesses kept authoring the key on unparsed intakes* — **answered, right**: a `dead` ledger row warns on an unparsed intake, so those four files remain valid witnesses that the ledger loaded; the tree walk excludes them by name with the reason, not by allowlist.
4. *PR body stale on one line (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED vs exit 0 on the final run)* — **answered**: the body text is the dev's evidence prose; this record judges from the head's check-runs, not that line. The adopting seat applies the dev's correction text if it edits the body; no verdict weight.
5. *First pre-push of the ADR commit refused for a card trailer* — process note on the companion branch; no effect on this diff.

`out_of_scope_findings`, each routed:

- *#2776 item 6 pointer* (ruling item 2's last clause) — belongs to the Tier H D11 PR / the PM, not this diff. **Escalated to the adopting seat**: confirm the pointer lands with the companion, since this PR cannot carry it.
- *objectui follow-up card* (ruling item 4: filed by seat 3 to the objectui lane now, not after this PR lands) — **not verifiable from this record's inputs**; escalated to the adopting seat to confirm the card exists before the queue. Until it lands, a Studio author who picks a value gets the 422 prescription on save (pinned here), and stored rows heal on read; no runtime exposure.
- *`skills/objectstack-data/references/lint-rules.md:23`* lists the removed rule — Tier H (`skills/**`), correctly NOT touched by this PR. **Escalated**: the row deletion belongs with a governed PR (the companion #23443 is the natural carrier).

Other flags from this review:

- **Test Core (3/6) and (4/6) in progress** at read time (named above). The record's verdict is on the completed set; the adopting seat does not queue on it until both conclude `success`.
- The PR is a **draft** at the head; the `Fixes #23268` line and `Clause-②: no` are present; `Part-of PR must not also close its card` and `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` are green, consistent with the companion using `Refs`.
- Docs Drift Check (advisory) flags 11 release-owned pages — read-only and untouched, as required.
- Out-of-repo consumer population and cloud stored rows: NOT MEASURED, stated in the changeset and the body; the cloud seat pointer (ruling item 5) is present.
